headline: After a frigid, foggy break tonight into Saturday, a fast-moving storm brings 2–8 inches of Sierra snow Sunday and another arrives Tuesday night or Wednesday, so the best pre-Thanksgiving travel windows are Saturday and Monday afternoon through Tuesday evening.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Isolated snow showers linger this afternoon, including a band off Lake Tahoe affecting communities east of the lake, before the storm exits and skies clear tonight. With fresh snow, clear skies and light winds, lows plunge into the single digits in Sierra valleys, with a few below-zero readings in the coldest spots such as Bridgeport and Bodie, and even western Nevada valleys drop into the teens. Freezing fog has a 40% chance of forming in the Mono Lake Basin, Carson Valley and Carson Sink, and is likely (80% chance) in the Martis Valley around Truckee and I-80 and in the Sierra Valley.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday is dry but cold, with highs about 15 degrees below normal and cold air trapped in the valleys, making it one of the best travel days. A fast-moving storm arrives Sunday (snow may start Saturday night at Sierra airports and late Sunday morning in western Nevada); it has little moisture and weak winds, so the cold air stays put with snow down to the valley floors, though in a warmer scenario snow levels could rise to about 5,000 feet by mid-afternoon Sunday. The likely range is 2 to 8 inches in the Sierra, far less than the recent storm but enough to make travel home Sunday evening difficult.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Monday afternoon through Tuesday evening is the best window to avoid snowy mountain drives before Thanksgiving. The midweek storm arrives sometime Tuesday night to early Wednesday with a decent supply of Pacific moisture but winds from the south, which raise temperatures and snow levels and limit how much snow spills east of the Sierra crest; it is not a major storm but will be disruptive during one of the year's busiest travel periods. The Friday after Thanksgiving looks clear, though about 70% of model scenarios hint at more Sierra snow sometime Saturday through Monday (Nov. 28–30).

watch_for: Single-digit to below-zero lows and freezing fog in Sierra valleys tonight into Saturday, including the Mono Lake Basin and around Truckee.
Sunday's 2–8 inches of Sierra snow making Sunday evening travel difficult.
Timing of the midweek storm (Tuesday night to early Wednesday) and its higher snow levels during Thanksgiving travel.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in tonight's clearing and cold and in Sunday's modest snow, less sure of exactly when the midweek storm arrives, and see no clear dry or stormy periods in the uncertain outlook beyond Thanksgiving.
